title: finding(i18n): the sync `resources` merge and the async `addResourceBundle` loader disagree on array values — replace vs index-wise, latent until a pack gains an array
body:
Spotted while implementing #7572 (the `createI18n` deep merge) — **not fixed there**, that PR's fence is the synchronous `resources` path. Filed unassigned.

## Two merge paths into one instance, two different array rules

`packages/i18n` installs caller-supplied translations through two paths, and after #7572 they agree on every value shape that exists today but not on arrays.

| path | who | array rule |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `createI18n({ resources })` — synchronous | `deepMergeTranslations` in `packages/i18n/src/i18n.ts` | **replaces** the array |
| `addResourceBundle(lang, 'translation', res, true, true)` — the provider's async loader, `packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx` (two call sites) | i18next's own `deepExtend` | **recurses index-wise** |

i18next 26.4.0, `dist/cjs/i18next.js:93` — `deepExtend` recurses whenever neither side is a string, arrays included:

```
if (isString(target[prop]) || ... || isString(source[prop]) || ...) {
  if (overwrite) target[prop] = source[prop];
} else {
  deepExtend(target[prop], source[prop], overwrite);
}
```

So a 2-element override onto a 5-element base leaves the base's last 3 entries in place — a hybrid list that neither side wrote. The synchronous path deliberately does not copy that; the reasoning is in #7572's PR body and in the `deepMergeTranslations` doc comment.

## Dormant today, and measured as dormant

**No built-in pack carries an array value**: walking all ten loaded packs, every leaf is a string (0 arrays, 0 non-string leaves). So the two paths are observably identical right now, and this is a latent divergence, not a live defect — which is why it is filed rather than folded into #7572.

It stops being dormant the moment any pack, or any app bundle served through the loader, gains an array value. Then the same override produces different results depending only on whether it arrived synchronously through `resources` or asynchronously through `GET /api/v1/i18n/translations/{lang}` — with nothing at the call site to say which.

## Not judged here

Whether to converge the two (teach the async path the same replace rule, e.g. by pre-merging before `addResourceBundle` rather than delegating the depth to i18next), or to leave the divergence documented and add a gate that fails if a pack ever gains an array value, is a design question. The second is cheaper and keeps i18next's behaviour untouched; the first removes the class. Left to triage.

Related: #7572 (where this was found and correctly fenced out).
